subject: Ordering a bar chart using non unique factor labels

messages.author: 273c069a7f0b8538
messages.subject: Ordering a bar chart using non unique factor labels
parts:
Alright so I'm trying to make a 4 paneled bar chart with each showing the top tfidf values and words for it's group. I also want the bars to be in descending order based on the tfidf. I've gotten it to kind of work but some of the values are getting messed up because some of the pages share words in their top 20 and therefore their factors are not unique. I've included the code and chart below. Any way around this? 

final_counts  %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  arrange(tfidf, .by_group=TRUE) %>%
  mutate(rn = row_number()) %>%
  # mutate(words = factor(words, levels = rev(unique(words)))) %>%
  top_n(20, rn) %>%
  ungroup %>%
  ggplot(aes(tfidf, reorder(words, tfidf), fill=id, alpha=tfidf)) +
  geom_barh(stat = "identity", show.legend=FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Highest tf-idf words in Wikipedia Page",
       y = NULL, x = "tf-idf") +
  theme_tufte(base_family = "Arial", base_size = 13, ticks = FALSE) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.6, 1), guide = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand=c(0,0)) +
  theme(legend.title=element_blank()) +
  theme(legend.justification=c(1,0), legend.position=c(1,0))+ 
  facet_wrap(id~., scales="free") + 
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90, hjust=2)) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

messages.subject: Re: Ordering a bar chart using non unique factor labels
parts:
I'm not sure to understand properly your issue given there's no dataset with your example. anyways, have you tried to use 

interaction function to define new unique factors for your ranking ? for instance you could define interaction(factor_used_already,facet_group_values) so in each facet the factors are unique ;) 

M.
